blocks.x: Why deal with seemingly endless rounds of job interviews when you can get hired right on the spot?!

New York City’s Administration for Children’s Services (ACS) is hosting a series of on-the-spot hiring events this October. The agency is rapidly recruiting Youth Development Specialists to work in its juvenile detention facilities, offering qualified candidates conditional job offers before they even leave the building.

For job seekers, it’s a rare opportunity to secure stable city employment, comprehensive union benefits, and a starting salary of $55,075—without needing a college degree or living within the five boroughs.
Here’s what applicants need to know about the role, the benefits, and how to secure an invitation to the October hiring events.
What does a Youth Development Specialist do?
Youth Development Specialists provide 24/7 care, safety, and direct supervision for youth (ages 10–24) in custodial settings whose cases are pending in Family or Criminal Courts.
Rather than sitting behind a desk, Specialists are actively engaged with the youth, serving as mentors and role models. Daily responsibilities include:
Providing safe and secure supervision within a highly structured environment
Facilitating daily schedules, including escorting youth to classes, meals, and recreation
Managing conflicts and youth behavior using de-escalation and Safe Crisis Management (SCM) techniques
Supporting youth in developing social, academic, and vocational skills

Pexels / Marina Abrosimova
Salary & benefits
The position offers a starting salary of $55,075, with annual increases bringing the total compensation to approximately $69,762 after five years (including longevity pay and uniform allowances).
Because this is a city government role, employees are inducted into DC 37—New York City’s largest public employee union—and receive a robust benefits package:
Healthcare: A choice of 11 health plans for individuals and families, including options with no co-pays or deductibles
Retirement: Access to the NYC Employees’ Retirement System (NYCERS) pension plan for guaranteed lifetime income, plus optional 401K, 457, and ROTH IRA plans
Paid Leave: Up to 12 paid holidays per year, plus vacation time (accruing 8:45 hours monthly) and sick leave (accruing 5.50 hours monthly)
Student Loan Forgiveness: Eligibility for the federal Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) program, which clears remaining direct loan balances after 10 years of qualifying payments
Additional Perks: Overtime pay at time-and-a-half, pre-tax transit benefits, and flexible spending accounts for medical and dependent care
Who is eligible to apply?
To broaden the applicant pool, the ACS has waived the standard New York City residency requirement, meaning applicants from outside the five boroughs are welcome to apply.
Candidates must be fluent in English, pass a mandatory background check and drug screening, and meet one of the following educational and experience requirements:
Academic coursework in social work, criminal justice, psychology, or related fields can also be substituted for experience (12 credits equals six months of experience)

A high school diploma (or equivalent) AND one year of full-time experience working directly with youth or young adults in a relevant setting (e.g., community services, educational settings, detention, mentorship, sports/athletics, mental health, or military service)
An Associate’s degree (or 60 college credits) AND six months of the experience listed above
A Bachelor’s degree in any field (no prior experience required)

Unsplash / Scott Graham
How to register for the hiring event
Unlike a traditional job fair, these on-the-spot hiring events are by invitation only.

Interested candidates must complete an online interest form in advance. The ACS will review submissions and contact qualified applicants to schedule a preliminary phone interview within 60 days. Selected candidates will then receive an official invitation detailing the time and location of the in-person event.
Note: To secure permanent city employment status, hired candidates will eventually be required to take and pass the official DCAS Civil Service Exam for the Youth Development Specialist title.
Don’t forget NYC also just opened a new Jobs Center to connect New Yorkers with high-paying roles.
Don’t miss out! Follow us on Facebook, Instagram, and now on WhatsApp, too!
